title: Custom Hooks
description: Learn how to create reusable logic with custom hooks.

data.text: **Custom hooks** let you extract component logic into reusable functions. They start with `use`, can call other hooks, and let you share stateful logic across components without repeating code.
A custom hook is just a JavaScript function whose name starts with `use` and that calls other hooks inside. It can return anything: a value, an object, or an array.

data.title: useCounter Hook
Hook Rules
items: Only call hooks at the **top level** — not inside loops, conditions, or nested functions.
Only call hooks from **React functions** — components or other hooks.
Start custom hook names with `use` so linters can enforce the rules.

data.title: Why the Rules?
data.text: React relies on the order of hook calls to associate state with the correct hook. Breaking the rules causes state to become corrupted or lost.
Encapsulate the entire fetch pattern — loading, error, data — into a single reusable hook.

Good Candidates for Custom Hooks
items: Data fetching with loading and error handling.
Any logic duplicated across multiple components.

terms.definition: A function starting with `use` that encapsulates reusable stateful logic.
Constraints ensuring hooks work correctly: top-level calls only, inside React functions.
Combining multiple hooks inside a custom hook to build complex behavior.

data.title: Exercise: Build useToggle
data.description: Create a custom hook that toggles a boolean value.
steps: Create useToggle(initialValue) that returns [value, toggle, setTrue, setFalse].
Use it in a component to toggle a modal open and closed.
Add a reset function that returns to the initial value.
data.expectedOutcome: A reusable toggle hook that simplifies boolean state management across components.

items.question: Can custom hooks share state between components?
items.answer: No. Each call to a custom hook creates its own isolated state. To share state, use Context or a state management library.

items.question: Do custom hooks need to start with use?
items.answer: Yes. The `use` prefix signals to React and linters that the function follows the Rules of Hooks.

items.question: Can custom hooks call other custom hooks?
items.answer: Yes. Hooks can be composed. You can build useLocalStorage using useState and useEffect, then use it inside another custom hook.

items.question: Where should I store custom hooks?
items.answer: In a `src/hooks/` folder, one file per hook (e.g., `src/hooks/useFetch.jsx`).

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Custom hooks extract reusable logic into functions starting with `use`.
They can call any other hook, including other custom hooks.
Follow the Rules of Hooks: top level, inside React functions only.
Common hooks: useFetch, useLocalStorage, useToggle, useWindowSize.
data.takeaway: Custom hooks are the secret to clean, reusable React code. Next, you will learn about Context and Refs to manage global data and DOM access.
